items.title: Fatal crash that killed four happened when car went out of control
items.summary: Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the Axia was travelling from Gerik towards Jeli when the crash happened about 1.30pm. He said the vehicle crashed into the rear of a Proton Persona, which was travelling from Jeli towards Gerik. Alwi said four occupants of the Axia, comprising two men, a woman and a child, were confirmed dead.

items.title: Sabah gives more than 500 adults second chance to learn reading, writing, counting
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 4 — More than 500 adults in Sabah who missed out on formal education are being given a second chance to master basic reading, writing and counting (3M) skills through the Functional Literacy Education Programme (PLF) organised by the Community Development Department (KEMAS). Sabah KEMAS director Ahmad Fakhrul Azman Muhammad Radzi said the participants are attending 25 classes this year in urban fringe, rural and remote areas across Kudat, Kota Marudu, Kota Belud, Keningau, Tenom, Nabawan, Beluran, Sandakan, Kinabatangan, Lahad Datu, Semporna, Tawau and Kalabakan. Before joining the classes, participants sit for a pre-test to assess their initial reading, writing and counting skills.

items.title: Kelantan authorities captured 36 stray dogs, including where boy, 8, was mauled
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Local councils in the state have captured 36 stray dogs this year, with most of the animals rounded up in Bachok, including the Kemasin area where an 8-year-old boy was recently attacked. State Local Government, Housing, Health and Environment Committee chairman Hilmi Abdullah said the operations were carried out between January and last week. "As of October, 36 stray dogs have been captured.

items.title: Yong Peng schoolgirl murder: Victim buried in Batu Pahat
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: The Form Four pupil who was believed to have been murdered at a school in Yong Peng was laid to rest at the Kampung Parit Arshad Muslim cemetery, here. The body of Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal arrived at her grandmother's house in Kampung Parit Selamat, Yong Peng, at 6.30pm after a post-mortem examination at Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital (HSNI) here. Earlier, the 16-year-old suspect who was detained at 7pm yesterday was remanded for six days by the Batu Pahat magistrate's court.

items.title: Mercedes-AMG brings V8, electric firepower as F1 returns to Malaysia
items.summary: MERCEDES-Benz Malaysia has brought two very different interpretations of high-performance motoring to the local market with the new Mercedes-AMG GT 63 Pro 4Matic+ Coupé and a preview of the all-new AMG GT 63 four-door coupé. V8 Power, Track-Focused Hardware The GT 63 Pro is powered by AMG's 4.0-litre V8 biturbo engine producing 450 kW, or 612 hp, and 850 Nm of torque. Power is sent through AMG's Speedshift MCT 9G transmission and fully variable AMG Performance 4Matic+ all-wheel drive.

items.title: Anwar: F1 excitement at Sepang also brings opportunities for local traders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — The return of Formula 1 (F1) to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after a nine-year absence has not only delighted motorsport fans but also provided an opportunity for about 40 local traders to earn an income through the Karnival Litar Rasa Madani. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the carnival, held at the G Hillstand at SIC in conjunction with the 2026 F1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP), brought together local traders offering a variety of food and beverages, including snacks and light refreshments. He said that the lively atmosphere at the circuit also gave visitors an opportunity to enjoy local fare while watching the race and, at the same time, supporting local traders.

items.title: Brazil votes in nail-biter polls closely watched by Trump
items.summary: BRASÍLIA: Brazilians headed to the polls on Sunday in a toss-up race between President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro that will decide whether Latin America's biggest nation follows a regional swing to the right championed by US President Donald Trump. He is facing a tough battle from right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year sentence for attempting a coup after his failed 2022 re-election bid. Lula has an advantage in Brazil's poor northeast, and among low-income voters, Catholics, and women.

items.title: UiTM difficulties must push institution to improve, says Zambry
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) must use the challenges it faces as a catalyst to improve rather than allow them to undermine the institution. Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said weaknesses within the university must be addressed openly, with efforts focused on strengthening the institution and ensuring its graduates become nation builders. UiTM has come under scrutiny after a former UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd group chief executive officer was charged with criminal breach of trust involving RM37.37 million.

items.title: Zahid proposes quantum technology department at UiTM by next year
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi wants Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) to establish a quantum technology department by next year to produce specialists in the emerging field. The deputy prime minister said the move would help ensure Malaysia keeps pace with developed countries in quantum technology. Present were Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir, Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and UiTM Board of Directors chairman Tan Sri Mohd Khamil Jamil.

items.title: Zahid urges UiTM to establish Quantum Department, says Malaysia must not lag
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 4 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has called on Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) to establish a Quantum Department to ensure the country does not lag behind current advancements. Ahmad Zahid, who is also the Rural and Regional Development Minister, said this after officiating the ‘Wacana Semarak Patriotisme: Seminar Ilmuwan Islam’ at the university’s Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor here today. Ahmad Zahid said his ministry would also contribute RM500,000 to UiTM to support the development of programmes such as the TVET UiTM Dihatiku training and certification programme and UTAMA PLUS UiTM AI Certified, including the development of the Quantum Department.

items.title: [UPDATED] BN to announce Melaka election partners after Oct 7
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Barisan Nasional will announce its choice of partners for the Melaka election after the Election Commission's announcement on Oct 7, its chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. "We will wait for the Election Commission's announcement on Oct 7. Meanwhile, Zahid said BN had drawn up plans to mobilise its election machinery and build a "blue wave" in Melaka.

items.title: Malaysia eyes F1 calendar return as PM Anwar confirms talks under way
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Malaysia is discussing a possible return to the Formula One calendar beyond this weekend’s race at Sepang, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today, raising hopes of a longer-term revival of the Malaysian Grand Prix. Anwar confirmed the talks during a brief exchange with Sky Sports commentator Martin Brundle on the grid at the Sepang International Circuit ahead of today’s Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The remark is the clearest indication yet that Putrajaya is considering extending Malaysia’s renewed association with Formula One beyond this weekend, which marked the sport’s first race at Sepang in nine years.

items.title: BN open to Pas using its logo in Melaka, but no decision yet
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Barisan Nasional is open to Pas using the BN logo if they cooperate in the Melaka election, but no decision has been made, said coalition chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi had previously said his party was open to using the BN logo in the Melaka election should there be cooperation with the coalition. The question over which logo Pas could use comes amid the suspension of Perikatan Nasional activities.

items.title: Brunei Sultan departs after witnessing F1 Gulf Air Bahrain GP return to Sepang
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 4 — The Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, departed for home today after concluding his special visit in conjunction with the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC). Earlier, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah attended the F1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at SIC with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and the top leaders of Malaysia, Bahrain and Brunei to witness the return of the prestigious F1 race to Sepang after a nine-year absence. Also attending the race were Bahrain Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

items.title: BN still open to cooperation with PH in Melaka
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Barisan Nasional is still open to working with Pakatan Harapan in the Melaka election, says its chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said this when asked whether BN was still willing to discuss cooperation with PH. Meanwhile, Zahid said BN's grassroots machinery would work alongside its eventual coalition partner throughout the campaign for the 16th Melaka state election.

items.title: Boy mauled by pack of five stray dogs in Bachok receives rabies jab, shows signs of recovery
items.summary: The boy’s mother, Rosnani Mat Salleh, 46, said her son, Azuar Firdaus Zuraiman, showed positive progress today after remaining withdrawn for two days as he was still traumatised by the incident. Recalling the incident, Rosnani said Azuar Firdaus was playing on the beach around 9.30 am with three relatives when five stray dogs approached. Rosnani said her son underwent a five-hour surgery the day after the incident to treat his injuries.

items.title: Amanah says Pakatan open to partners to form stable Melaka govt ahead of state election
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 4 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is open to seeking allies to form a stable government in Melaka in the upcoming state election, said Amanah secretary-general Muhammad Faiz Fadzil. He said Amanah’s stand was that it was better for the coalition to find partners who could work together to form a stable state government. Muhammad Faiz said any decision on political cooperation would be determined by the PH Presidential Council, but Amanah had been exploring collaboration with various parties.

items.title: Putrajaya Line resumes normal operations after cable theft
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Putrajaya MRT Line resumed normal operations at 1.27pm today after repair works following a cable theft incident near Taman Equine Station were completed. Rapid KL said the restoration of power supply allowed trains, which had previously been disrupted at Taman Equine Station, to resume normal operations. "The service will be reassessed based on operational requirements at the time," Rapid KL said in a statement today.

items.title: Water in RON95 tank claim: Checks find no contamination at petrol station
items.summary: BATU KAWAN: The Penang Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry has found no evidence of water contamination in RON95 storage tanks at a Batu Kawan petrol station following a viral complaint. State ministry director S. Jegan said inspections were conducted jointly with the oil company and station operator after a social media post alleged vehicle problems following refuelling. He said physical inspections of the pump area and tank sump also found no water accumulation apart from normal condensation.

items.title: Eight areas record unhealthy air quality
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Eight areas across Johor, Negri Sembilan and Sarawak recorded unhealthy air quality as of 5pm. In Negri Sembilan, Nilai recorded an API reading of 146 and Seremban 139, while Samarahan in Sarawak recorded 119. Only three areas recorded good air quality: Sandakan, Kangar and Langkawi.

items.title: Man dies after suspected electric shock while stealing cable
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: A man died after he was believed to have been electrocuted while stealing a Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) cable along Jalan Acob, Kapar, Klang, about 10am today. Klang Utara police chief Assistant Commissioner Ramsay Embol said police were alerted by a member of the public who found the man's body at the scene. "Police also found cable-cutting equipment and a motorcycle believed to have been used by the man at the scene," he said in a statement.

items.title: Don't let Melaka election rivalry affect national stability, says Johari
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Political parties must not allow rivalry in the Melaka election to turn into quarrels that could undermine national stability, says Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. Speaking after attending the Raintree Invitational tennis tournament at the Raintree Club Kuala Lumpur, Johari said stability was essential for economic growth and investor confidence. Johari said political alliances could shift, but rivals must maintain order.

items.title: Senior citizen loses RM113,550 in phone scam
items.summary: The 69-year-old victim, who panicked after being told he was involved in the illicit activity, withdrew money from automated teller machines (ATMs) before depositing it into unknown bank accounts. Jerantut police chief Superintendent Noor Azman Yusof said the victim received a phone call from someone posing as a policeman on Sept 11. "The caller told the victim that he was involved in money laundering activities.

items.title: Anwar: Malaysia discussing F1 returning to Sepang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government is actively discussing the possibility of having Malaysia back on the Formula One (F1) calendar. Speaking to Sky Sports commentator Martin Brundle during a live pre-race grid walk at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), Anwar said this was being looked into. Anwar, who was soaked after heavy rain drenched the circuit earlier, said he was nevertheless excited by the return of F1 action to Sepang.

items.title: MARC Ratings raises red flag over Zetrix AI's governance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MARC Ratings has revised the MARCWatch status on Zetrix AI Bhd to "Negative" from "Developing", citing growing concerns over the company's transparency and governance. The rating agency said it still lacked key information to assess the company's credit profile despite repeated requests. MARC Ratings said the revision to MARCWatch Negative reflected an increased likelihood of a rating downgrade.

items.title: Woman killed, man injured as car crashes into road barrier
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: A 28-year-old woman was killed when the car she were travelling in crashed into a road barrier along the Kota Iskandar highway here, today. Johor Fire and Rescue Department operation commander Saifulnizam Salleh said seven rescuers were deployed to the scene following the 10.54am distress call. Upon arriving they found the car had veered off the highway near a new development project along Jalan Bukit Indah-Puteri Harbour before crashing into the barrier.

items.title: Loke to hold press conference tomorrow on MYEG, Zetrix suspension
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Transport Minister Anthony Loke will hold a press conference tomorrow morning on the Road Transport Department's (RTD) suspension of My E.G. Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd as collection agents. Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd as collection agents would be suspended effective Oct 5.

items.title: Another woman files report against motivational speaker as Perlis police probe alleged sexual harassment
items.summary: KANGAR, Oct 4 — Perlis police have confirmed receiving another report against a male motivational speaker over an allegation of sexual harassment. Perlis police chief DCP Hamzah Hashim said the report was received yesterday and involved a 19-year-old female complainant. He said the motivational speaker would be released on police bail before being re-arrested by Kangar police for further action.

items.title: 52 foreigners detained in late-night raids on seven KL entertainment outlets
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Immigration officers detained 52 foreigners in late-night raids on seven entertainment outlets in the Dang Wangi area. The Kuala Lumpur Immigration Department said the operation, dubbed Op Gegar, began at 1.30am and involved 74 of its enforcement officers, supported by 18 from the department's Special Tactical Force (Pastak). In a post on its official Facebook page, the Kuala Lumpur Immigration Department said 170 people were screened during the operation.

items.title: India police investigate sexual harassment allegations during protests
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian police launched an investigation on Sunday into allegations of sexual harassment against officers during protests in the capital against the country's election commission. The harassment allegations were made on Saturday when police detained scores of protestors around the government-designated protest site of Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. "Allegations of sexual harassment were made by three female journalists against police officers," Delhi police said in a statement, promising "a fair and impartial enquiry."

items.title: Motorcycle skids towards drain near Taiping, killing 76-year-old rider
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 4 — An elderly man was killed and a woman who was the pillion rider was seriously injured after the motorcycle they were riding skidded at Lorong Kampung Boyan 1, Kampung Boyan near Taiping, today. Perak Fire and Rescue Department Assistant Director of Operations Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the 76-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene by Ministry of Health (MOH) medical officers. Sabarodzi said firefighters lifted the male victim, who was nearly falling into the drain, before MOH medical officers confirmed his death.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan joins Johor on unhealthy air list as haze lingers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — A total of eight locations recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the unhealthy category as of 4pm today. According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, five areas in Johor were affected, involving Segamat (156), Batu Pahat (155), Kluang (152), Tangkak (151) and Larkin (111). Meanwhile, 57 areas were in the moderate category, while three areas recorded good readings.

items.title: F1 roars back at Sepang as Sultan Ibrahim, Bahrain and Brunei royals watch on
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 4 — The return of Formula 1 to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after a nine-year absence received special attention today when His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, attended the 2026 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix F1 race, together with the top leaders of Malaysia, Bahrain and Brunei. His Majesty was received on arrival at about 2.15 pm by Bahrain Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Also attending the race were the Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, and Prince Abdul Mateen Bolkiah, who were received by Anwar at about 2.35 pm.

items.title: Empty nets in Latin America as fish flee El Nino
items.summary: FISHERMEN along Latin America's Pacific coast are reeling in half-empty nets as ocean warming aggravated by El Nino causes tuna, anchovies and other top catches to migrate to cooler waters. From Ecuador and Peru in South America, to Panama and Guatemala in Central America, some skippers have stopped going out altogether as fish stocks dwindle close to shore, in seas running at up to six degrees Celsius above normal. "The water is warm," Juan Ollague, 56, told AFP in the southwestern Ecuadoran port of Santa Rosa where hundreds of idle fishing boats are crammed into a small port.

items.title: 4, including baby girl, killed in East-West Highway crash [WATCH]
items.summary: GERIK: Four people, including a baby girl, were killed in a three-vehicle collision along the East-West Highway (JRTB) from Kelantan towards Gerik here today. The victims comprised two men, a woman and a baby girl. Gerik Fire and Rescue Station chief Mohd Rais Mahmud said the department received a distress call about the accident at 12.56pm.

items.title: Russia strikes hit Kyiv as Germany's Merz visits
items.summary: KYIV: Russia struck a bridge in Kyiv on Sunday soon after Germany's chancellor arrived in Ukraine's capital on a surprise visit to demonstrate European support in the face of an upsurge in attacks. Air raid sirens blared across Kyiv, urging residents to shelter, soon after Friedrich Merz's arrival under tight security, with warnings of approaching Russian attack drones. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has repeatedly urged Ukraine's Western allies for more military support, including advanced interceptors to shoot down Russia's new fast-moving, jet-powered drones.

items.title: After F1 and KL Marathon, October’s only getting busier with Melaka election dates on Wednesday and Budget Friday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — October has got off to a positive start for Malaysia, marked by a vibrant sporting calendar, strong performances by national athletes and encouraging developments in the economy and investment, while several major national agendas await as the month unfolds. The first weekend of the month saw Malaysia become a focal point for sports fans as the roar of Formula 1 (F1) machinery once again echoed at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after nine years, with Malaysia hosting the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026. Malaysia’s investment momentum also received a boost as the country and Singapore explored efforts to attract third-country investors to the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ).

items.title: Iran FM tells US there is no military solution to their conflict
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday that there was no military solution to his country's conflict with the United States, with talks on ending the war apparently at an impasse. A campaign of heavy bombardment failed to bring a decisive close to the war launched by the US and Israel in late February, and Washington in recent weeks has dialled back military operations in favour of economic pressure. "There is no military solution, nor any solution based on new sanctions," he continued, adding "only negotiations based on justice and fairness" could end the conflict.

items.title: Mubarak: Melaka election may indicate whether GE16 will be called early
items.summary: KUANTAN: The upcoming Melaka election could serve as an indicator of whether the 16th General Election (GE16) will be called earlier, said the Council of Former Elected Representatives (Mubarak). Its president, Tan Sri Abdul Aziz Abdul Rahman, said the current political momentum and Barisan Nasional's strength could be factors influencing the timing of the next general election. "GE16 needs to be held sooner, given BN's current strength.

items.title: King attends F1 Bahrain Grand Prix at SIC
items.summary: SEPANG: The return of Formula 1 to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after a nine-year absence received special attention today when His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, attended the 2026 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix F1 race, together with the top leaders of Malaysia, Bahrain and Brunei. His Majesty was received on arrival at about 2.15pm by Bahrain Crown Prince sand Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Also attending the race were the Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, and Prince Abdul Mateen Bolkiah, who were received by Anwar at about 2.35pm.

items.title: Petros assurance rings hollow amid challenge to Petronas, says Zaid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Former law minister Datuk Zaid Ibrahim says Sarawak premier Abang Johari Openg’s assurance that Petros will not undermine Petronas rings hollow while the state oil company seeks a bigger role in the gas business and Sarawak continues to question the federal legal framework governing petroleum. Writing on Facebook, Zaid said the central issue was Petros’s desire to take over the gas aggregator role currently performed by Petronas in Sarawak. He estimated Petronas’s Sarawak gas business at about RM10 billion annually.

items.title: JPJ hunts illegal motorcycle ride operators ferrying passengers to Sepang F1 circuit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) is tracking down individuals and groups offering illegal motorcycle ride-hailing services to transport visitors and spectators attending the Formula One (F1) Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC). According to Berita Harian , the operators were found advertising their services through various social media platforms, offering rides from several locations to the circuit grounds and between SIC and nearby parking areas. A survey of social media postings showed that both car and motorcycle transport services were being promoted, although motorcycles appeared to be the preferred option among spectators seeking to avoid heavy traffic congestion around the circuit.

items.title: Loke says resignation timing agreed with Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said the timing of his resignation, which will take effect once former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak pays the RM50 million fine, was agreed with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim when he tendered his resignation. I leave," said Loke, who is the transport minister, in an interview with The Straits Times. Loke said DAP would never take Chinese support "for granted", but added that the party must build consensus with its coalition partners.

items.title: Government to follow legal process over Bandar Utama school stabbing suit, says deputy law minister
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 4 — The government will allow due process to take its course following a civil suit filed by the family of a 16-year-old girl who was killed in a stabbing incident at a school in Bandar Utama last year, Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M. Kulasegaran said today. Asked whether existing laws should be strengthened to include mental health provisions, Kulasegaran said the government was not currently drafting any new legislation on the matter. He also stressed the importance of helping parents better understand their children’s needs, including mental health concerns.

items.title: Water in the tank at Batu Kawan? Penang team looks into viral claims of vehicle trouble after refuelling
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 4 — The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) in Penang is investigating claims that several vehicles experienced problems after refuelling at petrol stations near Batu Kawan. “The Penang KPDN has taken note of the claims of vehicles experiencing problems after refuelling at a petrol station near Batu Kawan. Earlier, several posts went viral on social media alleging that vehicles experienced problems, including being unable to start, after refuelling at several petrol stations around Penang.

items.title: Brother under seven-day police remand after Terengganu man’s death
items.summary: KUALA BERANG, Oct 4 — A man suspected of murdering his elder brother in Kampung Banggol Tasek, Bukit Payong, Marang yesterday has been remanded for seven days from today until Oct 10. The remand order for the 42-year-old suspect, a person with a mental disability, was issued by Kuala Terengganu Court Assistant Registrar Yuhanis Mohd Roslan at Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital (HSNZ) today to facilitate further investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder. Terengganu police chief Datuk Mohd Khairi Khairudin said today that dissatisfaction with his elder brother, who allegedly frequently asked their parents for money, is believed to have led to the fatal attack.

items.title: Rapid KL adds eight more shuttle buses as MRT Putrajaya Line repair work continues
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Repair works are underway to restore power supply and train services on the Putrajaya Line following a cable theft near the Taman Equine MRT Station, according to Rapid KL. It said alternative train services and free shuttle buses remained available to help passengers get to their destinations during the disruption. “Alternative train services and free shuttle buses are still operating to assist passengers, with eight additional buses deployed to facilitate passenger movement,” it said in a statement.

items.title: Raincoat and umbrella check: Storm warning for KL, Putrajaya and six states until 4pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and six states until 4 pm today. A similar warning was also issued for Kelantan (Pasir Puteh and Bachok) as well as Terengganu (Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus and Kuala Terengganu). In Sarawak, the affected areas are Limbang (Limbang), Miri (Marudi), Sri Aman (Sri Aman and Lubok Antu), Betong (Betong), Bintulu (Tatau), Sibu (Selangau) and Kapit (Song).

items.title: Consulate: Malaysians must enter Southern Thailand legally if they plan to get married there
items.summary: SONGKHLA, Oct 4 —Malaysians planning to get married in southern Thailand have been reminded to enter the country through legal routes and with valid travel documents to ensure that a confirmation letter can be issued by the Consulate General of Malaysia in Songklha. Malaysia’s Consul General in Songkhla, Ahmad Fahmi Ahmad Sarkawi, said that if they entered the country illegally, such as through unauthorised routes, the consulate would not be able to issue the confirmation letter due to violations of Thai immigration laws. He added that the consulate’s confirmation letter was important for court procedures related to the registration of the marriage in Malaysia.

items.title: Fadhlina vows full review after student’s death in Yong Peng, says MOE will cooperate with police probe
items.summary: YONG PENG, Oct 4 — Education Minister Datum Seri Fadhlina Sidek today said the Ministry of Education (MOE) will conduct a thorough review of all matters under its purview following the death of a student in Yong Peng, Johor, while police continue their murder investigation. In a Facebook post, Fadhlina said she travelled to Yong Peng this morning to personally obtain updates on the incident and received briefings from the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the Johor Education Department (JPN), the Batu Pahat District Education Office (PPD), and the school involved regarding the chronology of events and actions taken so far. She also met the victim's family at Hospital Sultanah Nora Ismail in Batu Pahat, expressing condolences and stressing that the family deserved answers regarding the tragedy.

items.title: Missing 77-year-old found dead after car plunges into Sungai Petani river
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 4 — The body of an elderly man who went missing after the vehicle he was driving skidded off the road and fell into a river at Jalan Lubuk Segintah-Lubuk Kawah here was found at 9.15am today. Kuala Muda police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan said the body of Mat Yusof Hashim, 77, was found between 50 and 100 metres from where his vehicle was located in the river. “The victim was fully clothed when found.

items.title: Money row emerges as suspected motive in Terengganu man’s death, brother under remand
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 4 — Dissatisfaction with his elder brother, who allegedly frequently asked their parents for money, is believed to have led a mentally challenged man to attack and beat his brother to death in Bukit Payong here yesterday, police said. Terengganu police chief Datuk Mohd Khairi Khairudin said police received information about a fight at a family home in Kampung Banggol Tasekat at about 10.55am. He said initial investigations found that the 43-year-old victim, the suspect’s elder brother, died after being allegedly beaten with a blunt object, while the suspect’s 36-year-old sister was also injured when she tried to stop the attack.

items.title: From F1 to the World Cup: How Anwar is using sport as diplomacy to put Malaysia on the world stage
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s approach of leveraging sports as a platform for diplomacy, economic activity and nation branding is helping position Malaysia back on the global sporting stage, according to an analyst. Global Peace Institute, London senior fellow Prof Dr Mohd Mizan Mohammad Aslam said Malaysia had, in recent months, demonstrated how global sporting events could be used not only to entertain the public but also to strengthen international relationships, generate economic activity and create a sense of shared national excitement. Mohd Mizan said Malaysia’s hosting of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix from Oct 2–4 demonstrated the international dimension of sports diplomacy, after the Bahrain Grand Prix could not proceed at its original venue due to geopolitical conditions in West Asia.

items.title: Anwar orders ‘immediate, thorough and transparent’ probe into Yong Peng student’s death
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has expressed his condolences over the death of secondary student Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairoul Faisal, whose body was found with injuries at a school in Yong Peng, Johor, yesterday. Anwar also directed the authorities to conduct an immediate, thorough and transparent investigation to determine the cause and establish what actually happened. In the incident at about 5.30pm yesterday, Irene Sofiya, 16, was found dead with injuries on her body, believed to have been murdered in a secondary school hall in Yong Peng.

items.title: Cable theft disrupts MRT Putrajaya Line, with longer waits at UPM, 16 Sierra and Putrajaya Sentral
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Train services on the MRT Putrajaya Line are experiencing delays following a power supply disruption caused by a cable theft incident near Taman Equine Station, according to Rapid KL. Following the disruption, passengers are expected to experience longer waiting times on platforms, particularly at UPM, 16 Sierra and Putrajaya Sentral stations. Shuttle trains between 16 Sierra and Putrajaya Sentral stations are operating at seven-minute intervals, the statement said.

items.title: Johor exco tells Education Dept to cooperate fully with investigators after Yong Peng student’s death
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 4 — The Johor State Education Department (JPNJ) has been told to extend full cooperation to assist investigations into the death of a Form Four female student at a secondary school in Yong Peng, Batu Pahat, yesterday. State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said JPNJ and the District Education Office should also provide the necessary support to the victim’s family and the affected school community. He said the state government viewed the incident seriously, especially as it involved the safety and welfare of students within the school area.

items.title: Lahad Datu deputy police chief Jimmy Panyau dies at 53 after liver-related complications
items.summary: LAHAD DATU, Oct 4 — Lahad Datu deputy police chief Supt Jimmy Panyau died last night at the Kuching Life Care Society in Sarawak after suffering from liver-related complications. Lahad Datu police chief ACP Dzulbaharin Ismail, when contacted, confirmed the death and said Jimmy, 53, died at 9.30pm. Dzulbaharin said the Iban officer had sought treatment at Borneo Medical Centre in Kuching on Aug 14 after experiencing liver-related health problems.

items.title: Murdered schoolgirl was well-liked, good student, says friend
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Oct 4 — A Form Four student found dead in a secondary school in Yong Peng yesterday was among the school's top academic performers and had been expected to achieve straight As in her Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination next year, according to a classmate. The friend said the 16-year-old victim's absence during an extra class session had initially raised little concern among classmates, who assumed she was unwell. Describing the victim, the friend said she was highly focused on her studies and actively involved in school activities.

items.title: Not a great day to be outdoors in Batu Pahat, Segamat and Kluang as API hits unhealthy levels
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Six areas in Johor and one in Sarawak recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels as of 9am today. In Sarawak, Samarahan recorded a reading of 152. Fifty-seven areas recorded moderate API readings, while three areas were at good levels, namely Sandakan (45), Langkawi (37) and Kangar (32).
